## Natural history notes

A crustose lichen characterized by a thin gray to olive-green thallus dotted with many tiny black, peppercorn-like fruiting bodies. In Florida, it is found growing on smooth bark in humid subtropical habitats such as hammocks, swamps, mangroves, shaded forests, parks, and other wooded areas with moist bark surfaces. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, growing tightly attached to bark and absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air rather than feeding on the tree itself.
